answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network applies topological cut verifications across transaction graphs to detect identity clusters. Clustered nodes must deposit stake into an auditing oasis pool. Randomly assigned auditor cliques engage in game-theoretic multi-agent auditing, triggering stake slashing if deceptive branches diverge. A willow protocol prunes correlated identities, creating a ripple of penalties that imposes superlinear attacker cost O(N^2).
